page: Microsoft Azure DS14_v2 is a DSv2-family virtual machine configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs and 112.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 7.0 GB per vCPU. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this server utilizes Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The CPU configuration features 16 physical cores with single-threaded execution per core, supported by a cache hierarchy consisting of 48 KB L1d, 1 MB L2, and 48 MB L3 cache. Local storage is bundled with a 229 GB capacity, and the instance does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile characterized by average multi-core capabilities and weaker single-core execution. The single-core performance is categorized as weak, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1247.29 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1105.0. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression (21.45 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (8.36 GB/sec) also fall into the bottom 25% tier. Conversely, multi-core and parallelized execution metrics are consistently average, as demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 19931.94, a Geekbench multi-core score of 9422.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 17133.93. Memory bandwidth is stable, recording 104.56 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 47.28 GB/sec for large-block write operations.

The DS14_v2 presents a clear tradeoff between single-threaded processing speed and memory capacity. While single-core computational throughput is limited, the high memory density of 112.0 GB provides qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require high-frequency single-core performance. In database and transactional operations, the server achieves an average PassMark database score of 8750.78 and handles 23.36 million Redis SET operations per second. Large-language model inference benchmarks show average performance for small and medium models, though text generation for a small 135M model is strong at 269.93 tokens/second. This hardware profile is appropriate for relational databases, memory-cached key-value stores, multi-threaded software compilation, and general-purpose enterprise applications requiring substantial memory allocations.
